<thought>To identify which elements can be definitively recognized from the observed isotope pattern, I retrieved the standard isotopic distributions. The spectrum shows a dominant peak at m/z ≈ 199, a very strong peak ≈ 2 Da higher (≈ 201) with intensity comparable to the base, and much weaker peaks at +4 Da and beyond. This pattern—strong M and M+2 peaks with roughly a 1:1 intensity ratio—is characteristic of bromine (⁷⁹Br and ⁸¹Br). No other common element shows such a pronounced M+2 peak at this intensity (chlorine gives a 3:1 ratio, sulfur’s M+2 is only ~4 %). Therefore, bromine can be definitively identified. No other element’s isotopic signature is unambiguously present. 

The required answer is a list containing only bromine. 
</thought>
<final_answer>['Br']</final_answer>
